title: Smoke: history holds a correction, the present turn only asks for a recap
capability: A message was corrected two days ago. Today the person only asks for a recap. The recap uses the corrected wording, the superseded wording never reaches the Provider, and no Trust Action is triggered. This is the wrong-Action clue from #312: asking to look back is not asking to correct.

allowed.statement: The presentation for the customer is on Thursday morning at ten, with the deck half finished.
After work there was a short run on the treadmill that ended at about twenty minutes.

forbidden.statement: Placing the customer presentation on Wednesday afternoon at three, which is the superseded wording.
Asking the person which of the two timings is right, or offering to change a record.

topics.statement: Stress over an unfinished deck for a customer presentation.
A short treadmill session after work.

time.statement: Both were said on 10 September local time, two days before the question.

expectedBehavior: Recap both subjects in the person's mixed register.
Use the corrected Thursday timing without remarking that it was changed.
failureSignals: The superseded Wednesday wording reaches the Provider or the reply.
A correction or other Action is admitted for a plain recap request.
The reply turns into a clarification about which timing is right.

sourceEligibility.reason: Superseded by the person's own correction; only the current revision may be used.
Retained original expression inside the default background.

criteria.description: The recap request streams and commits.
The corrected wording reaches the Provider.
The superseded wording never reaches the Provider.
The uncorrected message from the same day still reaches the Provider.
No Action is admitted for a plain recap request.
First visible text within 3 s and the complete reply within 10 s (CLI network).
The recap covers both subjects, uses the corrected timing and places them two days back.
